packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04 - unverified image reading

Exposure / compliance statement
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author for this packet.
- I opened only PROMPT.md (identical text in each packet; read once in packet-01) and the image files of this packet. One directory listing of my three assigned packet directories was run to learn filenames; packet.json was not read. No web or search.

WORKING NOTES (appended tile by tile)

image-001.jpg (reduced overview)
- One face of a parchment fragment, c. 12 x 13.5 cm by the scale, upright as presented; left edge torn with a projecting tongue at lower left; oval hole right of centre; several small holes; reddish-brown spatter at upper right. Surface almost entirely rubbed/washed: the main area carries only ghost traces of text lines.
- A vertical stain/rule line c. 1.2 cm in from the left edge separates a narrow left zone holding small cursive writing (line ends? or marginal note) from the main field.
- Upper right: a row of bold black letters each with a macron, read "ā ā ā ā ā" (five), and below it, about 1.3 cm lower, two more "ā ā" - these are in a heavier formal hand than anything else on the face.
- Right edge, mid-height: a faint rectangular stamp-like impression (vertical lettering, not readable at this reduction).

image-002.jpg (native tile, upper left)
- Left zone, small cursive brown-ink writing, cut by the torn left edge; 5-6 short lines:
  image-002 l.1  ]ribus   (or "]tibus"/"]cibus"? - "…ibus" certain)
  image-002 l.2  ]l(?)… t(ur)?   (tall letter + letters + a looped final sign like -us/-ur; not securely readable)
  image-002 l.3  ]…e(?)us?   (4-5 letters with a final looped abbreviation; [illegible])
  image-002 l.4  ]…ecu(m)?   (letters "eci"/"ecu" + hole; uncertain)
  image-002 l.5  ]…y(?)i   (two or three strokes only)
- Main field of this tile: only grey smudges where lines stood; a few pen traces near centre-right (below the bean-shaped hole) of 2 short lines, [illegible] (perhaps "…"/"…ibus"?).

image-003.jpg (native tile, upper right)
- image-003 l.1  ā ā ā ā   (CORRECTION to the overview note: at native resolution there are FOUR letters, each a formal gothic "a" with a horizontal bar above; bold black ink, slightly blurred. Nothing else on that line survives to left or right.)
- image-003 l.2  ā ā   (two more of the same, c. 1.3 cm lower and slightly to the right, partly under rust-coloured spots)
- Tentative interpretation only: these barred letters are much larger and blacker than the ghost text and stand isolated; they could be residue of a different layer (e.g. offset or the only surviving ink of a line), or pen trials. No connected text.
- Rest of tile: red-brown spatter; at the bottom edge faint reddish hairline pen-flourish traces (penwork? observation only), no letters readable.

image-004.jpg (native tile, middle left)
- Left zone (left of the vertical stain line with holes), faint grey traces at the torn edge:
  image-004 l.1  ]… (two rounded letters, "oa"/"aa"? at c. 55% height) [illegible]
  image-004 l.2  ]…uc? / ]…ac?   (at c. 95% height: 2-3 letters, "inc"/"uc"?)
  image-004 l.3  a red mark/letter at the very bottom left edge (red ink trace, shape like a paraph or "R"?), unreadable.
- Main field: abraded; surface flaked. Isolated ink remnants only:
  right side at c. 70-80% height, next to the oval hole: traces of one line "…a…ls"? [illegible], and below it two detached strokes resembling "s"/"ſ" and "z"/"2".
  further down "…in…"? [illegible].
- No word can be read with any confidence in this tile.

image-005.jpg (native tile, middle right; overlaps 003 at top and 004 at left)
- Centre-left above the oval hole: 5-6 short ghost lines, of which only flaked ink islands remain; the surface shows fine reddish hairline hatching (possibly remains of penwork flourishing around a lost initial - tentative). No letter sequence recoverable: [illegible] x 6 lines.
- Left of the hole, two lines of ink remnants (same as image-004): "…" then "…a…ls"? [illegible].
- A vertical crease/rule runs down the tile about two-thirds across; to its right the surface is blank apart from rust spots.
- Lower right: a blind (uninked or very faint) rectangular stamp, c. 1.5 x 4 cm, set vertically, with two columns of capital letters reading sideways; individual letters not legible (shapes like "B", "E", "S", "O"?). Appears to be a later ownership/library stamp, not manuscript text (tentative).

image-006.jpg (native tile, lower left)
- Blank brown parchment with small slits and a fold; a red trace at the upper left edge (same red mark as image-004 l.3). The projecting lower-left tongue enters at left edge. No text readable. [illegible/blank]

image-007.jpg (native tile, lower right)
- Blank/abraded parchment; a horizontal tear running in from the right edge; in the upper part a few flaked ink islands and reddish hairline traces continuing those of image-005. No letters readable. [illegible/blank]

SUMMARY

Layout (observation): single face, upright as shown; text almost wholly lost by abrasion/washing (the fragment looks like the worn outer side of a binding cover or pastedown). What survives:
 (a) a narrow strip at the far left edge with small cursive writing in brown ink, 5-6 short line-ends at the top (image-002) and scattered letters further down (image-004); whether these are line-ends of a lost column to the left or marginal notes cannot be decided from the images;
 (b) ghost lines in the main field (several short lines above and left of the oval hole) of which no word is recoverable;
 (c) six isolated bold barred letters "ā ā ā ā" / "ā ā" at upper right;
 (d) a blind vertical stamp at the right edge;
 (e) a small red mark at the left edge (mid-lower).
 No running title, rubric, enlarged initial or underlining can be confirmed; reddish hairline traces near the hole might be penwork (tentative).

Readable text, complete list:
  image-002 l.1  ]ribus   ("…ibus" secure; preceding letter r/t/c?)
  image-002 l.2-5  uncertain fragments as noted above
  image-003 l.1  ā ā ā ā
  image-003 l.2  ā ā
Everything else: [illegible]. No connected span of prose could be transcribed from this face; this reflects the state of the leaf (ink gone, surface flaked), checked tile by tile at native resolution.

Areas not covered at native resolution: the projecting tongue at lower left (visible only in the overview image-001, where a line of small cursive writing runs along its upper edge, c. 3 cm long, not legible at that reduction: possibly "…uine(?) … mo…si…"? - not usable).

Limitations / suggestions
- The other face of this fragment (not in this packet) is likely to carry the readable text; a multispectral or raking-light image of this face would be needed to recover the ghost lines.
- A native-resolution crop of the lower-left tongue would be worth adding.
- Orientation is taken from the left-edge cursive lines and the barred letters, which both read upright as presented.
